ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: NAVIQUAL-XR: Finding the Sweet Spot of a Live Music Environment in Augmented Reality
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.28056v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Augmented Reality (AR) enables immersive spatial audio experiences that extend conventional stereo and head-tracked listening to six degrees-of-freedom (6-DoF) navigation. However, evaluating listener Quality of Experience (QoE) remains a key challenge due to the real-time and dynamic adaptations of the content in AR environments. To address this challenge, we propose NAVIQUAL-XR, an objective model to find the "sweet spot" in AR live music environments validated by subjective tests. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Granary-v2: Scalable Multilingual Speech Data Curation for Predictable and Controllable Model Outputs
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.28248v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speech-language models that follow instructions need training data that connects the same recording to different output forms and tasks. We present Granary-v2, a multilingual speech dataset and reusable curation system that provides a data foundation for these models. Granary-v2 extends Granary-v1 with aligned transcript variants and instruction-target pairs for multi-task speech-language training. Language coverage increases from 25 to 48 languages. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Preserving Prosody in Speaker Anonymization
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.28290v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Effective prosody modeling is essential in natural speech generation applications, but complications arise in speaker anonymization, since speaker attributes are present in acoustic correlates of prosody. Our work aims to improve previous reported tradeoffs between effective speaker obfuscation and preservation of prosodic content. To this end, we integrate an existing pretrained privacy-preserving prosody encoder into a speech synthesis model, enabling prosody-preserving speaker anonymization. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Speech Emotion Recognition Across Languages: Prosodic Patterns and Self-Supervised Learning
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.29040v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This study investigates the prosodic patterns of emotional speech across Chinese (CN), German (DE), and English (EN), with a focus on acoustic characteristics. Using ANOVA and mixed-effects modeling, we reveal cross-linguistic and emotion-specific prosodic patterns. A comparative analysis of Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) performance demonstrates that humans outperform Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) models in cross-lingual tasks, while SSL models show significant improvement in cross-lingual SER through an efficient fine-tuning process, achiev

ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Voice Agents: From Auditory Intelligence to Auditory Agency
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.29465v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Voice systems increasingly combine streaming speech, persistent state, reasoning, tool use, and embodied control. Once these functions share a runtime, spoken input can change digital or physical state, and recognition or response quality alone no longer characterizes the system. This article studies the interfaces through which spoken evidence becomes consequential. \emph{Auditory intelligence} denotes the capabilities required to perceive, understand, coordinate, and generate spoken interaction; \emph{auditory agency} denotes the causal path f

ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: S$2$SCORE: A Textless Unified Evaluation Metric for Speech-to-Speech Translation Systems
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.29557v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Evaluating speech-to-speech translation (S$2$ST) systems requires assessing multiple dimensions of translated speech, including semantic adequacy, speaker similarity, and acoustic naturalness. Existing approaches are largely text-based, relying on ASR transcripts and primarily assessing semantic adequacy, while other dimensions require separate metrics. We propose S$2$SCORE, a unified text-free evaluation framework that jointly models these dimensions within a multi-task architecture and produces a human-calibrated overall quality score. S$2$SCO

ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Characterizing Frozen SSL Encoders and Backends for Cross-Domain Speech Deepfake Detection
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.29865v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) encoders are the dominant front end for speech deepfake detection, and the prevailing recipe fine-tunes the full encoder on a small spoofing corpus, maximizing in-domain accuracy at the cost of known degradation under domain shift. Taking a recent cross-attention fusion of SSL and constant-Q cepstral features as a fixed reference recipe, we freeze its encoder and ask which encoder and which backend behave best across domains. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Which Layer to Trust? Layer Selection in Frozen Speech Encoders for Singing-Voice Deepfake Detection under Signal Corruption
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.29871v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Frozen self-supervised speech encoders have been frequently used for audio deepfake detection. However, the layers are usually chosen from a development set. We examine this choice for singing-voice deepfake detection on CtrSVDD. We train one detection head per layer, plus a learned layer mix, on frozen XEUS (3-4 seeds) and XLS-R (2 seeds). We test on clean audio and under noise, reverberation and lossy coding. On clean audio, the middle layers beat the last layer in both encoders and the learned mix does not beat the best single layer. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: BiSAT: Bidirectionally Aligned Semantic-Acoustic Tokenization for Speech Language Models
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.30723v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speech language models (LMs) generate speech as sequences of discrete tokens. Their tokenizer must therefore preserve both acoustic detail and linguistic content at a low bitrate. Semantic-enhanced tokenizers may lose acoustic detail, whereas acoustic-oriented tokenizers retain acoustic variation that makes language modeling harder. Unified tokenizers combine both, but representing acoustic detail and linguistic content within a single feature space can cause interference between the two objectives, and existing approaches typically align acoust

ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: SpeechSplice: Pronunciation Control in Encoder-Decoder LLM-based TTS by Replacing Encoder Hidden States
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.30927v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Most large language model (LLM)-based text-to-speech (TTS) methods offer no explicit function for correcting pronunciation. Consequently, these systems frequently mispronounce many everyday words, such as proper nouns, heteronyms, numerals, and domain-specific terms. While weight-editing or fine-tuning can mitigate this, these solutions risk quality degradation and must operate offline. We propose SpeechSplice, a training-free encoder-output replacement approach for pronunciation control in encoder-decoder LLM-based TTS. SpeechSplice replaces th

ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: SoundFleXR: Selectively Constraining Axes of Audio Rendering Presentations
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.28020v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Extended reality (XR) systems increasingly rely on audio cues to help users locate, interpret, and interact with virtual content, especially when the content is outside the field of view. To support this, many systems use head-related transfer functions (HRTFs) to approximate real-world acoustics. However, a realistic simulation is only one possible presentation. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: REMORA: A Voice-First Memory Assistant for Grounded Personal Recall and Independent Living
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.28026v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Most of what matters in a day is spoken and written down nowhere: a dosing interval named at a clinic, a deadline moved in passing, the place a document was set down. Such information is consequential because it is operational, and fragile because it arrives during divided attention -- the moment its importance becomes clear is rarely the moment it was said. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.29315v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Generative voice cloning threatens voice-based authentication, yet current deepfake detectors rely on power-hungry, high-precision models unsuited to edge hardware. We present SWIFT (Streaming Whiten-Integer Forensic Trust-Engine), a handcrafted detector that works in the high-frequency noise domain where synthesis artifacts concentrate. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: LiveAudio: From Bidirectional to Autoregressive Diffusion for Real-Time Streaming Video-to-Audio Generation
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.30714v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Video-to-audio generation synthesizes sound that matches a video in content and timing, with applications ranging from film post-production to live streaming, games and interactive world models. Interactive applications receive video continuously and need the sound to follow it in real time, yet most existing video-to-audio models are bidirectional and must observe an entire clip before producing any sound. We propose LiveAudio, a streaming video-to-audio framework that generates high-quality and synchronized audio in real time while the video

ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Lightweight Detection and Model Attribution of Synthetic Speech via Residual Statistical Fingerprints
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2411.14013v5 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: As speech generation technologies advance, so do risks of impersonation, misinformation, and spoofing. We present a lightweight, training-free method for synthetic speech detection and source model attribution. Our method builds on model-specific fingerprints that are computed as the average of the differences between audio signals and their filtered versions, referred to as residuals. Leveraging the Mahalanobis distance of the residual for a given audio signal to these model-specific fingerprints allows to identify the source model as well

ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: PopMelodyGen: A Copyright-Aware Platform for Controllable Pop-Melody Generation
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.28686v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large-scale redistributable symbolic pop-melody data remain scarce due to copyright restrictions, creating a bottleneck for both practical deployment and reproducible research in music generation. We present PopMelodyGen, a copyright-aware platform for controllable pop-melody generation that combines rule-based synthesis with neural generation. Our approach first uses an expert synthesizer to produce large-scale labeled synthetic melodies from explicit musical knowledge and templates, providing scalable pretraining data with auditable provenance

ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: Training speech deepfake detectors against worst-case filters: Gains, Costs and Limits
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.28718v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speech deepfake detectors make few errors on standard benchmarks, yet a simple attack defeats them: the attacker passes fake speech through one short filter, tuned against the detector, and many fakes then pass as real. Training with random filters does not stop this attack, because the attacker uses the worst filter, not a random one.

ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: Beyond File-Level Splits: Rethinking Symbolic Music Evaluation via Multi-View Alignment
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.28765v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Symbolic music generation often continues MIDI passages by predicting subsequent notes or events. Held-out prediction loss can overestimate generalization to unseen compositions when training contains another performance or arrangement of a test work. We introduce Multi-View Alignment-Aware Same-Work Identification, combining complementary musical representations with temporal alignment of shared passages to remove test-work versions from training while preserving unrelated material and fixing evaluation files. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: Restorable Multilingual Voice Anonymization via Audio Watermarking
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.28863v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Voice anonymization aims to conceal speaker identity while preserving linguistic and paralinguistic information. However, certain applications also require the ability to attribute anonymized recordings to their original speakers. Existing recovery approaches often rely on specially designed reversible anonymization systems, limiting their applicability to different anonymization architectures. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.29012v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spatial audio large language models increasingly combine general audio understanding with spatial perception. Yet overlapping conversations require more than locating speakers. A model must also recover what each person says and match the words to their positions. We examine this challenge in MiDashengLM-Spatial, a binaural model designed for both spatial reasoning and general audio understanding. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.29085v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Partially spoofed audio embeds spoofed segments in a bonafide utterance, and spoof localization is the task of locating them. Most countermeasures (CMs) operate at the frame level. Typically, they include a front-end representing the audio as frames and a back-end classifying each frame as bonafide or spoof. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.29225v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Music creation is inherently iterative, yet many symbolic generation systems still center on producing or regenerating isolated outputs. We present IteraSong, an interactive web-based Digital Audio Workstation (DAW) for LLM-guided iterative symbolic music creation. Unlike one-shot generation systems, IteraSong supports a generate-audition-edit-refine loop over a persistent multi-track project. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.29226v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autoregressive text-to-speech (TTS) with continuous speech latents avoids quantization-induced information loss, but typically relies on a latent space that is learned separately and then frozen before language-model training. Such a space must satisfy two competing requirements: it must retain enough acoustic detail for high-fidelity reconstruction, yet be sufficiently structured and regularized to support autoregressive prediction by a language model. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.29283v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Adding a singing voice to an existing piano recording requires decisions about melody, syllable placement, pronunciation, timing, and vocal register. ARRANGE organizes this work as a sequence of agent skills with readable intermediate artifacts and composer approval checkpoints. An LLM translates instructions in plain English, notes played on a keyboard, and vocal references into local edits; deterministic scripts validate and apply those edits before open audio models render the result. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.29375v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Audio large language models (LLMs) are typically evaluated on song genre, mood, and instrumentation. A more basic skill is telling whether two short clips play the same melody, chord or instrument. We introduce MusicListenBench, a benchmark of paired listening tests for melody, harmony, timbre, and tempo. Each test item comes with two variants. A FLIP variant changes the music, so the answer must change. A STAY variant changes only the sound, such as room echo or hiss, so the answer must stay the same. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: Who Plays What: Same-Instrument Music Separation from Video
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.29411v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: When two musicians in an ensemble play the same instrument, they sound alike and their instruments look alike. Audio-only separators, and audio-visual separators that rely on appearance, cannot tell them apart. What still differs is how each player moves, and when. We study same-instrument per-player separation: a user clicks one musician in a video and receives that musician's sound alone, even when other players in the video play the same instrument. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.29475v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Musical style, a global attribute that functions throughout a whole piece, is a lever widely used by users in modern large music generation models. Yet how style is represented inside these models, and which components drive it, remains largely unexplored. In language models, circuit analysis traces a representation to a sparse sub-network of a few key components, namely attention heads and MLP neurons, and has been used successfully to explain and control global attributes such as emotion. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).title: Scoring L2 Pronunciation Without Synthesis: Counterfactual Velocity Contrast in Frozen Flow-Matching TTS
ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.29985v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Flow-matching text-to-speech (TTS) models learn how native speakers realize a text, yet this knowledge is used only for synthesis. We show that a frozen TTS model can score non-native (L2) pronunciation without generating audio. For a learner utterance, we compare the model's velocity-prediction error under the target text with its error under a counterfactual text (dropped or swapped) on the same noised input; the difference behaves like a generative goodness-of-pronunciation score. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.30049v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AIRPiano aims to bring sound to the common practice of rehearsing piano music on a tabletop. Guided by a known score, users make piano-like finger movements on a flat surface without reproducing absolute keyboard positions. The score supplies pitches, while hand motion determines which score events to play and when. We formulate this interaction as online alignment between tabletop hand motion and symbolic score events. CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Jamaica Suk, producer, DJ, and friend, has died
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
We lost Jamaica Suk yesterday, the singular musical force. To say this hits close to home is an understatement; few people have been a better friend or a greater inspiration. My thoughts are with her family, in particular, right now. Music in the end is just an excuse to spend some time together and share some hopes and dreams. Take care of one another. Here's the official statement.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Photophore 2, a 100-oscillator iOS/AUv3 flock synth twelve years in the making
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
Photophore renders a swarm of one hundred oscillators as a flock navigating a three-dimensional habitat. First seen on CDM in 2014, version 2 of Taika Systems' instrument adds AUv3 support on iOS -- and parameters modeling predators, hunger, and fear. The result is lush, nuanced layers of sound, pads to leads, that feels uniquely alive.

The post Photophore 2, a 100-oscillator iOS/AUv3 flock synth twelve years in the making appeared first on CDM Create Digital Music.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Nine Inch Nails fans can now stream nearly 2000 live recordings
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
NIN fans, it's a momentous week. For nearly 20 years, the Nine Inch Nails archive has been compiling live shows from 1988 to today; that's now nearly 2000 recordings of over 1200 concerts. The site is a pleasure to navigate now, and this week came big news: streaming, on demand.

The post Nine Inch Nails fans can now stream nearly 2000 live recordings appeared first on CDM Create Digital Music.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Korg’s phase8 acoustic synthesizer adds companion app, updated firmware
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
Korg's phase8 remains an acoustic, resonating fascination, just at a time when everything seems lost in a sea of software. The companion app we saw first at Berlin's Superbooth is now public this week, expanding sequencing capabilities and providing tools for arranging and storing ideas, alongside tweaked device firmware.

The post Korg’s phase8 acoustic synthesizer adds companion app, updated firmware appeared first on CDM Create Digital Music.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Seek sick sets from SITKA, Zuggamasta, hellocatfood, in cables and code
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
It may seem the world is closing in, the internet is dying, tides of slop are rising -- don't believe it. The underground shares signs of hope, from Kyiv's SITKA to Köln's Zuggamasta to Earth's hellocatfood. It's got modules. It's got (entirely human!) coding. It's got trippy visuals. The underground resists, nerd style, and it's all happening thanks to the Fediverse and the fantastic Brighton-based Gravitons.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Berlin’s largest electronic music venue, now a stage for debuting military AI
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
Berlin Kraftwerk, the former power plant in Berlin Mitte associated with Tresor and Ohm, was the venue last week for Helsing's launch of new agentic technology, Clarity. This platform uses the same controversial AI-driven approach implicated in accelerating the use of flawed intelligence and killing civilians in Palestine, Lebanon, and Iran. Kraftwerk's Head of Sales has taken sole responsibility and apologized. But the fiasco seems emblematic of Berlin's pivot from cultural capital to military-industrial capital, with the money that follows.

The masterful artist Ryo Fujimoto works in electronics not just as a passive actor behind machines, but fully embodied in physicality, voice, and sometimes screams. Ableton Live 13 is now in limited public beta. That includes a lot of what you've asked for, like multi-band Racks, overhauled preset navigation, and ARA 2 support for tools like Melodyne.
